replies.raw_markdown:
I can share my own experience here now that the solution is out.

For a long time I could not figure out how to improve it, because I just keep telling the agents to "try everything you can" to optimize TPS.

I did not thing of potentially just pruning of changing the serving until I came a cross a REAP Qwen3.8 model, and the idea crosses my mind and I started to explore the direction. It feels like an entire untapped area to explore.

To be fair to Astra and Claude, it seems that they do get better at inference engineering from the current version onwards. But regardless you still need to be the brain pointing the agent to high potential region for it to explore and achieve gains.

comments.raw_markdown:
Thanks a lot for putting this together, saves me a lot of time. 
Looks like I took a wrong turn with the context vs concurrency tradeoff. For the most part, I thought the decode throughput was the bottleneck, so I kept the concurrency high. The logs showed me that the kv pool sat somewhere between 91-97% full and requests queued for cache space, so the memory was the actual limit but I realized this a bit too late. Also, the fp8 kv was implemented yesterday and i spent the free memory on history (the trims moved from 37k->27k to 57k->45k). I guess this alone took the score from 14.5 to 22.5.

replies.raw_markdown: I didnt really compare the kv formats. fp8 was what pennyroyal's flash next receipe uses, and it halved the memory vs bf16, which i needed for longer history. I havent tried nvfp4 kv. For the nll check: at short contexts, it might not show what happens at 60k-100k tokens where we actually run. A token-matched run with only kv dtype changed would settle it. Also, my cleared levels used a median of around 0.8x the baseline actions (64% at or under the baseline). Some harness changes that helped were simply to not mislead the agent. (For ex: UNDO instead of ACTION7, "level restarted" instead of "game over",  removing lines that tell the agent to ignore the budget bar, etc etc,.)
